============================================================
Empirical Research Plan
“Does CSR Improve Firm Financial Performance?”
============================================================

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------
• Method: Sharp (preferred) / fuzzy (robustness) regression-discontinuity design (RDD) exploiting the 50 % majority-vote threshold for CSR shareholder proposals.  
• Why appropriate:  
  – The running variable (percentage of ‘For’ votes) is continuous and cannot be perfectly manipulated at the margin.  
  – The 50 % rule generates an as-good-as-random discontinuity in pressure on management to adopt the requested CSR policy, isolating causal effects from voluntary self-selection that plagues standard cross-sectional regressions.  
  – Abundant prior use of voting cut-offs in finance (e.g., Say on Pay, board elections) validates this design.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control Definition
------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
 Treated_it = 1 if proposal for firm i in meeting-year t obtains > 50 % of votes cast (Pass), 0 otherwise (Fail).

Control group  
 Observations with vote share just below 50 % serve as the counterfactual for those just above 50 %.

Timing  
 Event date: Annual meeting date in year t when voting result is announced.  
 Outcomes:  
 • Short-run: monthly abnormal stock returns in the [–3,+3] months around announcement.  
 • Medium-run accounting outcomes: fiscal year t (same year), t+1, t+2.  
  Primary window = fiscal year t+1 (allows time for implementation).

Running variable and cutoff  
 RV_it = %For votes minus 50.  
 Cutoff at RV = 0. The design is “sharp” for an ITT effect; we will show first-stage jump in actual CSR implementation (Δ KLD strengths) to justify sharpness and, if <1, implement fuzzy RDD (2SLS).

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff.  
 Plausible: marginal votes are unlikely to correlate with unobserved firm shocks.

A2. No precise manipulation of vote share at 50 %.  
 Plausible: individual shareholders and management rarely predict exact turnout; will be tested with McCrary density and “heaping” diagnostics.

A3. Local SUTVA / no interference.  
 Reasonable: one firm’s CSR adoption near the threshold has negligible impact on other firms’ outcomes.

A4. First-stage relevance (for fuzzy RDD).  
 Empirically testable: pass → jump in subsequent KLD strengths; historical evidence shows ≈20–30 p.p. jump.

A5. Functional-form correctness within chosen bandwidth.  
 Mitigated by non-parametric local-linear estimators and multiple bandwidth checks.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigations
------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Strategic manipulation of vote totals (e.g., management adjourns meeting).  
 • McCrary density test.  
 • Covariate smoothness (size, pre-vote performance, institutional ownership).  
 • Exclude meetings with multiple adjournments or recounts.

T2. Imperfect compliance—some passed proposals not implemented, some failed nonetheless adopted.  
 • Estimate ITT (sharp RDD) as baseline.  
 • Fuzzy RDD 2SLS: first stage = pass dummy, second stage = actual CSR implementation (Δ KLD).  
 • Report both ITT and LATE.

T3. Multiple proposals or serial correlation within firm.  
 • Cluster standard errors at firm level.  
 • Restrict sample to first CSR proposal within ±3-year window as robustness.  
 • Include firm and year fixed effects in difference-in-RDD panel extensions.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dimensional FE regressions
library(rdrobust)    # Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik RDD
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading --------------------------------------------
iss   <- fread("iss_csr_proposals_1997_2012.csv")       # vote data
comp  <- fread("compustat_1996_2013.csv")
kld   <- fread("kld_msci_strengths_1995_2013.csv")
crsp  <- fread("crsp_monthly_1996_2013.csv")

# 2. Variable construction -----------------------------------
iss[, rv := vote_for_pct - 50]                # running variable centered at 0
iss[, pass := as.integer(rv > 0)]             # treatment
# Merge outcomes
iss[, fiscal_year := year(meeting_date)]      # align to Compustat fiscal year
data <- merge(iss, comp,  by = c("gvkey","fiscal_year"), all.x = TRUE)
data <- merge(data, kld,  by = c("gvkey","fiscal_year"), all.x = TRUE)

# Dependent variables
data[, tobins_q := (mkt_val + debt_in_tot) / at]        # simple Q proxy
data[, roa       := ib / at]
# Later: abnormal returns using CRSP

# 3. Main specification (local linear, Calonico kernel) ------
bw <- rdrobust::rdbwselect(y = data$tobins_q, x = data$rv)$bws[1,"h_l"]
main <- rdrobust(y = data$tobins_q, x = data$rv, h = bw)

summary(main)

# 4. Fuzzy RDD (LATE using implementation) -------------------
# First stage: jump in CSR score
fs  <- rdrobust(y = data$kld_strengths, x = data$rv, h = bw)
# 2SLS via rdrobust's fuzzy option
fuzzy <- rdrobust(y = data$tobins_q, x = data$rv, fuzzy = data$pass, h = bw)

summary(fuzzy)

# 5. Robustness: different bandwidth and polynomial order ----
robust_small <- rdrobust(y = data$tobins_q, x = data$rv, h = bw/2, p = 1)
robust_large <- rdrobust(y = data$tobins_q, x = data$rv, h = bw*1.5, p = 1)
# Covariate balance test
cov_test <- rdrobust(y = data$assets_prevote, x = data$rv, h = bw)

# 6. Plot RD graph -------------------------------------------
rdplot(y = data$tobins_q, x = data$rv, binselect = "esmv")
```

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results (Prior)
------------------------------------------------------------
Theory is ambiguous (doing well vs. doing good), but meta-analyses lean positive.  
Prior: Firms just passing CSR proposals experience a modest improvement in valuation metrics.  
Magnitude:  
 • Tobin’s Q: +0.05 to +0.10 (≈ 1–2 % of mean).  
 • ROA: +10–20 bp.  
 • 3-year buy-and-hold abnormal return: +2 – 4 %.  
We also expect a clear first-stage jump in KLD strengths of ~0.3–0.5 s.d.

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
------------------------------------------------------------
C1. No sorting/manipulation at cutoff  …… 1  
C2. Covariate continuity around cutoff … 1  
C3. Correct functional form / bandwidth  … 1  
C4. Large enough effective sample size   … 1  
C5. Stable treatment (single intervention) … 0  (questionable due to imperfect compliance & heterogeneous CSR topics)

Overall score: 4 / 5 – design is highly credible but we remain cautious about treatment heterogeneity across proposal types.

============================================================
